claims.claim: SWI-Prolog 10.0.2 is installed as a native arm64-darwin executable and satisfies PeTTa's declared >=9.3 dependency.
The executed PeTTa source was fetched from the canonical repository and detached at ae66fa8e41dcd5539d614706bd4e5cfb34f9608d with a clean 230-file source manifest.
The minimal fixture produced final scalar 5 with exit 0 in two separate native executions with byte-identical stdout.
Changing only the expected scalar from 5 to 6 caused the verifier to fail with exit 1.
The standard PeTTa launcher invoked native swipl directly; the fixture and captured executable trace contain no Python or py-call seam.
CONSTITUTION.md, ACCEPTANCE.md, AUTHORITY_MAP.md, and POC_SPEC.md retained their entry hashes.

remaining_unproven_assumptions: G01 does not prove the MeTTa-to-Prolog import call or typed marshalling; that is G02.
G01 does not prove that later Miter workloads avoid every possible Janus/Python path; it proves only that this standard minimal execution does not invoke one.
Optional MORK and FAISS integrations were not built or selected.
